[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

A private data visualisation workshop with Datalabs Agency costs between $4,600 and $7,500 inc GST, depending on length and delivery format. Every price includes up to 12 attendees, so for a full team the per-person cost is well below public training classes. Full pricing, inclusions, and group-size options are below.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-icon" icon_size="30" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fa fa-solid fa-circle-arrow-down" show_icon="enable_icon" delim_line_color="#8224E31C" icon_color="#EEE6F6" icon_hover_color="#D4C9E0"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][vc_single_image image="52827" img_size="large" alignment="center" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The straight answer, up front..." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

How much does a data visualisation workshop cost in Australia?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Corporate data visualisation and data storytelling workshops in Australia generally cost $3,000 to $8,000 per workshop day for private groups. Datalabs Agency’s 2026 prices sit inside that range: $4,600 for a remote half-day through to $7,500 inc GST for a full day on site, including up to 12 attendees.

Datalabs Agency is a Melbourne-based data visualization consultancy founded in 2012 that delivers corporate training workshops (Power BI, Tableau, data storytelling), dashboard design, and BI style guides for clients including Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, and UPS.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Everything your team needs..." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

What is included in every workshop?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Every Datalabs workshop includes the facilitator, a tailored agenda from our ~16 workshop topics, an interactive workbook, 70 dashboard grid templates, and 18 downloadable dashboard icons. Workshops are led by our founder, who learned visual storytelling at National Geographic, and focus on design thinking rather than software mechanics.

That tool-agnostic approach means the same workshop works whether your team lives in Power BI, Tableau, Excel, or PowerPoint. Popular topics include Introduction to Data Visualisation & Storytelling, Designing Great Dashboards, Infographics & Report Design, and Creative Data Presentations with PowerPoint — see the full list on our training workshops page.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][dfd_button button_text="Get a fixed quote" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datalabsagency.com%2Fcontact-us%2F|||" icon_font="fontawesome" icon_fontawesome="fa fa-solid fa-basket-shopping" background="#707E65" hover_background="#2D3C23" border="border-style:hidden;|border-width:0px;border-radius:10px;" hover_border="border-style:hidden;|border-width:0px;border-radius:10px;" style="style_6" padding_left="60" padding_right="22" icon_size="20" icon_color="#FFFFFF" icon_hover="#00000000" title_font_options="font_size:16|line_height:48"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-12" width="1/3" offset="vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-table"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The current rate card..." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

Datalabs workshop price list (2026)

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

All prices are in Australian dollars, include GST, and include up to 12 attendees, the interactive workbook, and downloadable templates. Remote workshops run live on Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Webex; on-site workshops are delivered at your offices.

How does group size change the price?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Each workshop price includes up to 12 attendees. For groups of 13 to 20, add $250 per additional attendee per day, which covers their materials and keeps the session hands-on. Beyond 20 attendees we split the group into two cohorts rather than diluting the workshop.

Workshops teach best at 20 people or fewer — past that point, exercises and individual feedback suffer. Splitting a larger group into cohorts costs more than surcharging would, but both groups get the workshop that earns the feedback. Multi-team or multi-city rollouts are quoted as a single data visualisation training programme.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-table"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Bring the whole team..." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

Group pricing at a glance

What moves the price up or down?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Prices rise with extra attendees beyond 12, travel beyond Melbourne, and deep customisation — building exercises around your own datasets, dashboards, or brand guidelines, which is quoted as preparation work. Prices come down for multi-workshop series bookings and for choosing remote delivery over on-site.

If you are planning a series — the same workshop for several teams, or a progression across skill levels — ask for a programme quote. Series bookings attract a discount on subsequent sessions, and multi-city or multi-office rollouts are quoted as a single training programme rather than one-off workshops.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-table"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Three ways to learn..." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

Private workshop or public course — which should you book?

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-1"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Melbourne based, globally delivered..." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

Can you deliver a workshop in our city?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes. Datalabs workshops are delivered worldwide from our Melbourne base. On-site sessions have run in the United States, Germany (several cities), Saudi Arabia, Hong Kong, and Singapore, as well as across Australia. Travel is quoted up front with the workshop price, so international delivery arrives as one fixed, itemised quote.

Remote delivery crosses borders even more easily: workshops run live on Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Webex, and a full day can split into two mornings to suit your time zone. For in-person delivery the session fee is the same rate card shown on this page plus travel — no international premium hidden in the price. If your team is spread across offices or countries, ask for a programme quote.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" el_id="pat-faq"][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_column_text css="" item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

Questions & Answers

Workshop pricing

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="Is GST included in the prices?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes. All prices on this page are in Australian dollars and include GST. If you need an itemised quote for procurement — inclusions, attendee numbers, preparation hours, and travel listed separately — we provide one before you commit to anything.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Do you run workshops outside Melbourne?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes. Remote workshops run anywhere via Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Webex, and on-site workshops are delivered worldwide — recent sessions have run in Sydney, Canberra, Hong Kong, and Germany. On-site delivery outside Melbourne adds travel costs, quoted up front with the workshop price.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What if we have 30 attendees?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

We split the group into two cohorts and run two sessions — for example, morning and afternoon of the same day. Each cohort gets the full interactive workshop, and the second session is priced as part of a series rather than as two separate bookings.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Is there a cheaper option for small teams or individuals?" tab_id="1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes. Our self-paced online courses — An Introduction to Data Visualization and Storytelling, and Designing Great Dashboards — are $127 each in the Datalabs shop, and include the same design frameworks the live workshops teach.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How do we book a workshop?" tab_id="1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0"][vc_column_text css=""]

Send us your team size, preferred format, and rough timing through the contact form on this site, and we will reply with availability and a fixed quote. There is no phone tag and no obligation — you will know the exact price before you decide.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Do you offer government or not-for-profit rates?" tab_id="1786585600001-gov-rates-6q"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes — government and not-for-profit rates are available; mention your organisation when you enquire. Every quote is itemised for procurement, with inclusions, attendee numbers, preparation hours, and travel listed separately, and remote delivery works well for distributed teams. Recent government-sector sessions have run in Canberra.

Why we price per session, not per seat

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

Public training classes price per seat. Private workshops price per session. That single difference decides which one makes sense for your team, and it is why this page quotes session prices rather than per-person rates.

A public one-day class in Australia charges $395 to $622 per person. Send twelve people and you have spent roughly the price of a private full day — except the curriculum was generic, the examples were someone else’s data, and the date was fixed by the provider. A private session flips all three: the agenda is tailored from our ~16 workshop topics, the exercises can use your own dashboards and reports, and the workshop runs when your team can actually attend.

Per-session pricing also sets an honest ceiling on quality. Workshops teach best at 20 people or fewer; past that, the exercises and individual feedback that justify a live workshop stop working. That is why groups beyond 20 split into cohorts rather than paying a surcharge — and why the second cohort is priced as part of a series, not a separate booking.

I learned visual storytelling at National Geographic, and I have run these sessions for corporate teams for more than a decade. The best sessions are never the biggest ones — they are the ones where every attendee has built something with their own data by the afternoon. The pricing model exists to protect exactly that.

Who teaches these workshops?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

I started visualizing data at the National Geographic Society back in the early 2000s. A lot has changed since then. I took what I learned there — visual storytelling and infographic design — and applied it to my new world and new company Down Under.

I was one of the first to bring infographics to Australia. The problem was it was too early. No one at that time understood the power of that type of visual data and storytelling. Believe it or not, “What is an infographic?” was a typical question.

I was at the first Tableau roadshow in Melbourne, Australia. The speaker asked the audience of a thousand or so attendees, “Who here is currently using our product?” Roughly one in ten hands went up. Since then, Microsoft Power BI has overtaken Tableau, both in client interest and in functionality. I now design and teach in both — see our dashboard design page.

In the early days of the BI revolution, consulting with Marriott Hotels in Hong Kong, I saw a need for data visualization style guides. Too many dashboards are created without a design philosophy, without a common design language, and without proper attention to color theory, typography, grid systems, and user experience (UX) design. My data visualization style guides now operate inside companies such as Mercedes-Benz in Germany, Intel in San Francisco, BlackRock in New York, and Telstra in Australia.

What’s next in data visualization? I think you know where this is going: artificial intelligence. Where am I going with the Datalabs Agency? Same answer.

screen_normal_spacer_size="10" screen_tablet_spacer_size="10" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_column_text]Take the old business staple — the annual report. The annual report for most corporations and government bodies is a must, a yearly exercise of gathering data, collecting information, and producing a document that resembles the same basic report produced last year. Most likely, this is a printed document, flat, on a white background, with stock images sprinkled throughout its pages. It’s digital cousin, the PDF, is there for journalists, analysts, and shareholders to download.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="200" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="120" screen_tablet_spacer_size="110" screen_mobile_spacer_size="100"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_desktop:20|padding_right_desktop:20"][vc_column width="1/2" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" css=".vc_custom_1533713297304{padding-right: 30px !important;}" responsive_styles="padding_left_tablet:20|padding_right_tablet:20|padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="50" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" enable_delimiter="" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]Digital Annual Reports: The Future Format for Visual Communications[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="10" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="10" screen_tablet_spacer_size="10" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_column_text]Produce this old school annual report if you must. But take a look at Datalabs’ interactive annual reports & microsites or digital annual report. Your corporate communications story is told in interactive charts and graphs, animated videos, beautiful photographic and infographic imagery, and with text that wraps it all together. Datalabs works with your communications team on the content that you’d like to include in your microsite. We can work with your current report, which has just been published and bring it a new life online. Or we can work with a PDF or printed document from the past and develop and design it as a visual, multimedia microsite that will get noticed, used, and easily understood by your audience.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" css=".vc_custom_1533713309258{padding-left: 30px !important;}" responsive_styles="padding_left_tablet:20|padding_right_tablet:20|padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="50" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" enable_delimiter="" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]Our Year In Review Microsites & Digital Annual Reports Tell A Great Deal Of Information In Very Little Time[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="10" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="10" screen_tablet_spacer_size="10" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_column_text]Clicking on the navigation scrolls the user down the page, not to a separate website or page. Data is visualized, interactive, even animated. All within one online website. If you’re interested in designing a new corporate annual report or microsite and wanting to push your communications in an innovative and visual direction, contact us at Datalabs and inquire our interactive annual reports & microsites.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][dfd_single_image image="834" alignment_resolution="750"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row dfd_enable_overlay=""][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][dfd_heading style="style_02" subtitle="See a new way of reporting..." title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" subheading_margin="margin-top:10px;"]Examples of Our Digital Annual Reports & Interactive Microsites[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]

width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css="" el_class="p-c-2"]Our data visualization agency — led by our founder and Managing Director, Otto Ottinger — devises strategies that build insightful interactions between a company’s data and the employees in charge of acting on it. We make data look beautiful, easy to engage with, and quick to understand. And clients love it. They love the simplicity, the pursuit of beauty in business intelligence design.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="25" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css="" el_class="p-c-2"]To do this, we keep things simple: we offer analytics and data visualization products, like business intelligence dashboards, data presentations, animated data videos, and infographic reports. The Datalabs Agency has now infused artificial intelligence into its training and design workflows. Business and government can now tap into our agency's expertise in automation and strategic advice with AI.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="25" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="25" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading mobile_alignment="left" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" subtitle="Business and artificial intelligence design..."]A Data Visualization Design Firm That Simplifies the Complex[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="25" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css="" el_class="p-c-2"]As a first step, Datalabs audits the data sources that are being captured by a company, then we cleanse that data. Sometimes the structure of data isn’t pretty. Our data visualization agency will get its hands dirty, utilizing the best software available to simplify, reformat, and rebuild your company’s data. Once the data is in a tight and tangible format, we go to work building a story. Data can be creative. We honestly believe that. There are innumerable stories that are captured in CSV and XML files, you just have to look for them.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="25" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css="" el_class="p-c-2"]The Datalabs analytics and visualization team works with companies to “humanize” the numbers and equations that accrue inside spreadsheets and data feeds. Inside data, there are winners and losers, actors and events. Causality, proportion, and trends in data are the most important and vital information a company can have. And it needs to be understood, communicated, and acted upon. The story has to be memorable, compelling, beautiful, and most of all simple.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="25" screen_normal_resolution="1024" story excites and influences its audience. The growth of interest in and demand for infographics is a great example of visual storytelling moving into the mainstream. Data visualization techniques marry together the human forms of perception and understanding with data’s digital complexity and scale. Our design firm believes that in order to be successful in your job, whether it’s in Marketing, Manufacturing, Finance, or Politics, you have to be data-competent.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="25" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css="" el_class="p-c-2"]You have to be a storyteller. In other words, it’s great to have a hunch, but it’s even better to be able to prove it. Using the science of analytics and the artistry of data visualization, Datalabs can help you get there. Show us your data. And we’ll show you the magic and beauty that comes from numbers.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="25" screen_normal_resolution="1024" Clearer Messages." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Visual Storytelling for Government Employees: A Unique Training Workshop[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]In today's digital age, effective visual communication is crucial for government agencies to connect with their citizens. Visual storytelling and data visualization offer powerful tools to convey complex information in a compelling and accessible manner. Why shouldn't government employees embrace these techniques to enhance transparency, engagement, and decision-making? Visual storytelling is best at combining narratives with captivating visuals.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]For government employees, incorporating new techniques in design will enhance their ability to communicate key messages effectively. By leveraging images, videos, infographics, and interactive content, they can present data-driven narratives that resonate with the public. Visual storytelling not only simplifies complex information but also humanizes government initiatives, making them more relatable and engaging for citizens. Data visualization is an essential tool for promoting transparency within government agencies.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]By presenting data in easily understandable visual formats, employees can foster trust and confidence in government initiatives. Clear and accessible data visualization empowers citizens to explore information, track progress, and make informed decisions. Government employees should strive to use interactive charts, maps, and dashboards (so-called new data viz) to present data in an engaging and user-friendly manner, ensuring transparency and fostering an environment of openness. Storytelling with public policy data aids understanding and therefore, aids in the decision-making process.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]Government employees can utilize these techniques to analyze and interpret complex data, identifying patterns and trends that inform policy development. Artificial intelligence (AI) like Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, and Claude can help. Visualizing data allows decision-makers to grasp insights quickly and make informed choices based on evidence. By presenting data-driven narratives, government agencies can inspire confidence in their decision-making processes and demonstrate accountability to the public. It's that simple. And it's our hope that this workshop will move the dial of creative visual communications with data.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="65" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="65" screen_tablet_spacer_size="65" screen_mobile_spacer_size="65"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row]

Our Infographics Training Workshop

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]The Datalabs Agency’s Infographics & Report Design Workshop introduces the audience to the basic principles of data visualization and its common forms, language, influences, and formats. It focuses on infographic design, data, charting, and tools that we use in our day-to-day agency work and have developed over 15 years of designing infographics for clients in Australia, Asia, the United States, Europe, and the Middle East. We look at the modern use of generative AI in infographic design, both the good and the bad.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.expandIn" delimiter_settings="border-bottom-style:dotted;|border-bottom-width:1px;|width:100px;|border-bottom-color:#d2d2d2;" delimiter_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" style="style_02" subtitle="Over 15 years of experience" title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]

Infographics Workshop Taught by Professionals

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.slideDownIn"][/vc_column_text][vc_column_text]Infographics are one of the most popular forms of data visualization and are an increasingly used format for communication for government departments & businesses. Broadly, infographics cover a number of styles and formats — from reporting infographics to dashboards. Infographics are used everywhere now: in social media and direct marketing, on billboards, and in TV commercials. They're even ubiquitous as the design style for corporate and government documents, both internal and external.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="55" The training consists of classroom-style learning, theory and hands-on exercises that help the participants get in the headspace of an infographic designer, account manager, product manager, creative director or data visualiser. The interactive parts of the training included how to construct/deconstruct an infographic, how to prototype and plan an infographic, how to use data effectively in reporting, and how to tell a story – with or without data.

Lots of Infographics, but Very Few are Designed Well

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]Infographic design has been made easier with tools like Canva and Piktochart, but these tools do not teach the underlying principles of good infographic design. The result is that thousands of poorly designed infographics are published every day. Poorly designed infographics don't convey their message effectively and can even damage your brand or company's reputation if they contain incorrect data or information.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.expandIn" delimiter_settings="border-bottom-style:dotted;|border-bottom-width:1px;|width:100px;|border-bottom-color:#d2d2d2;" delimiter_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" style="style_02" subtitle="About this training for infographic design..." title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]

Software is Secondary, Design Thinking is Crucial

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]This workshop, developed by data visualization experts in Melbourne, Australia, is an introduction to the core principles of infographic design (visual hierarchy, colors & contrast, typography, etc.) as well as practical tips for designing effective graphics using popular software such as Adobe Illustrator and Canva. By the end of this workshop, you and your team will have a clear understanding of how infographics work as well as tips on where they're most commonly used in business today.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.expandIn" delimiter_settings="border-bottom-style:dotted;|border-bottom-width:1px;|width:100px;|border-bottom-color:#d2d2d2;" delimiter_margin="margin-top:30px;margin-bottom:0px;" style="style_02" subtitle="So do you..." title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]

Want to Learn How to Design Infographics?

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]We know that everyone has different learning styles, which is why we offer this infographic training as either a live workshop (on-site at your organization) or online (Microsoft Teams or Zoom). Our instructors are all experienced professionals who have worked on award-winning projects around the world – so they know exactly what makes great design work (and what doesn't). They'll show you step by step how to make sure every infographic tells its story effectively - no matter where it's published or viewed. So whether you're looking for better ways of communicating data internally within your organization, or want more effective tools for sharing reports externally with customers or clients - our screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="0" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][vc_column_text]Interactive infographics are designed to allow your audience to “play”, control, and see information in the form of online, animated graphics. Interactive charts, maps & cartography, and infographics embedded with multimedia can create a rich and unique experience. A higher-order form of visual content, interactive infographics have a bright future as a format for digital communication and reports. As the web world grows more visual, the Datalabs Agency thinks this is inevitable:  the flat infographics of today will evolve into interactive infographics tomorrow. The reason is simple: they are more engaging than their static cousins. Their design needs to consider how your audience will behave with the interactive structure of your story.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" enable_delimiter="" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h3|color:%23282828" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]Want to know what style of infographic is best for you? But through our simple design process, Datalabs takes the complexity away for our clients. Through a series of questions, our interaction designers tease out how your audience can get the most engaging and insightful experience with your information. Questions like:[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_icon_list main_style="style-1" icon_size="20"][dfd_icon_list_item icon_type="custom" icon_img="550"]How will your audience discover the interactivity of the infographic?[/dfd_icon_list_item][dfd_icon_list_item icon_type="custom" icon_img="550"]What information is shown when they roll over the data, the content?[/dfd_icon_list_item][dfd_icon_list_item icon_type="custom" icon_img="550"]How is this additional information designed, presented?[/dfd_icon_list_item][dfd_icon_list_item icon_type="custom" icon_img="550"]How will the graphics move, fade, enlarge?[/dfd_icon_list_item][dfd_icon_list_item icon_type="custom" icon_img="550"]…and finally: How will navigating across the interface work?[/dfd_icon_list_item][/dfd_icon_list][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text]Our designers are trained to create memorable experiences with each graphic we create. Infographics or infographic reports are used to visually present a company’s or government organization’s key ideas and insights. Reports, metrics, and KPIs will all look better visualized as infographic numbers and shared internally via your company's intranet, as collateral in meetings, or used to bolster a business case.

Cartography is the art and science of making maps… and making beautiful and informative maps is what our agency does. The Datalabs Agency has world-class map designers on staff with extensive experience in geospatial design and development.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]

Every day our agency handles large amounts of location data. Our map designs engage audiences on a avriety of devices: websites, tablets, and mobile applications, communicating the great stories of ‘where?’ using the best cartographic software available today.

We can work with your development team to design maps to embed in your company’s or government organization’s applications and websites. Datalabs also develops and designs maps for internal use, as well — maps that serve inside of your intranet, sales, or client reporting portals. All we need to know is what data would you like to see on a map and we’ll design a fantastic experience on a mapping platform and in a format that makes sense for your business.

Map Designers with Style

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]

Our agency has been designing and developing map experiences since 2011. Before that, our founder worked for National Geographic in Washington, DC, and Whereis.com in Australia. The cartographic development team at the Datalabs Agency works with Google Maps and other rich mapping libraries. Our vast knowledge of mapping platforms gives us an advantage — it helps us arrive at the best piece of technology, the best foundation to build a solid, well-designed map interface for our clients. See some of our favorite projects below.

Tips for Designing Interactive & Animated Maps

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-6" width="1/3" offset="vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-4" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)"][dfd_info_box module_animation="transition.slideLeftIn" icon="dfd-icon-map_way" line_hide="yes" style="style-01" layout="layout-06" title="Big Insights in Mapping" icon_size="45" icon_color="#000000" icon_hover="#999999" icon_bg_size="45" title_font_options="tag:h3" subtitle_font_options="tag:div" font_options="tag:div"]Sometimes the biggest insights in mapping are what’s not there: gaps, spaces, and distances. Visualizing the invisible often leads to the most insightful actions.[/dfd_info_box][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="85" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="85" screen_tablet_spacer_size="70" screen_mobile_spacer_size="50"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-6" width="1/3" offset="vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-4" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)"][dfd_info_box module_animation="transition.slideLeftIn" icon="dfd-icon-user_location" line_hide="yes" style="style-01" layout="layout-06" title="Vanity of the User" icon_size="45" icon_color="#000000" icon_hover="#999999" icon_bg_size="45" title_font_options="tag:h3" subtitle_font_options="tag:div" font_options="tag:div"]People see themselves in maps. Often they look for locations they are familiar with: their homes, their workplaces, and major landmarks to orientate themselves. Visualize Creatively in PowerPoint

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]Up-skill your team in the creative use of Microsoft PowerPoint, data visualization design, and visual storytelling. Get the confidence to influence and entertain your audience. It all starts with designing your data well and using storytelling to make it memorable. At the Datalabs Agency here in Melbourne, Australia, we believe that, in the proper hands, Microsoft PowerPoint could be used for the purposes of good, rather than evil! pages/18547.content:
[vc_row dfd_bg_style="image" dfd_bg_image_new="25274" dfd_image_bg_color="#e9e9e9" dfd_bg_img_attach="fixed" dfd_overlay_color="#e9e9e9" dfd_overlay_pattern="transperant" dfd_row_config="full_width_content" bg_type="image" bg_image_repeat="no-repeat" bg_img_attach="fixed" fadeout_row="fadeout_row_value" enable_overlay="enable_overlay_value" overlay_color="#ffffff" overlay_pattern="transperant"][vc_column dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_tablet:20|padding_right_tablet:20|padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="120" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="90" screen_tablet_spacer_size="65" screen_mobile_spacer_size="55"][dfd_heading style="style_02" subtitle="Beautiful Power BI reports..." title_font_options="tag:h1" subtitle_font_options="tag:h2"]Power BI Style Guides & Brand Guidelines[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]

Get data visualization design experts working on your brand's Microsoft Power BI reports.

Tableau style guides and brand guidelines save a huge amount of time when styling new dashboards. They also reduce the costs of retrofitting the existing designs.

Get consistency for your business intelligence, nail down a defined process for visualizing data, and determine — once-and-for-all — a clear style for your brand in Tableau.

Our Tableau Style Guides & Brand Guidelines set the visual standards for your company's dashboard layouts, user interface (UI) components, fonts, and charts, plus so much more... Take a look below and then get in touch with us.

screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Your analysts and data scientists are not graphic designers.

They’re not creative data visualizers, either. Then why expect them to design your company’s reports beautifully, simply, with a common user experience that is intuitively appreciated by your broad group of stakeholders? Get them a Tableau Style Guide designed with the help of your brand team and let that guide their visual aesthetic and usability ideas. A Tableau Style Guide lets them concentrate on what they do best: data analysis and insight generation.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][dfd_single_image image="25327" module_animation="transition.fadeIn"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row dfd_enable_overlay="" anchor="buy" css=".vc_custom_1597109536881{background-color: #e9e9e9 !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_column_text]

As a data visualization agency, we see it again and again: Companies spend time and money to redesign and re-style their Tableau dashboards. Why? Because there are no design standards.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_message message_box_color="warning" icon_fontawesome="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"]

Without a Tableau style guide, design standards do not exist.

[/vc_message][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_column_text]

Without a Tableau Style Guide, the lack of design standards:

1) negatively affects the user experience (UX) of your dashboard's audience. 2) gets very expensive 3) is not a strategic use of your BI resources.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_column_text]

With BI guidelines in place, you and your team will:

1) save time & effort designing dashboards and workbooks. 2) move seamlessly from dashboard concept to final design. 3) design on-brand .twbx files forevermore.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row css=".vc_custom_1644285898840{background-color: #e9e9e9 !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="50"][dfd_delimiter icon_size="10" delimiter_height="3" delimiter_border_style="dotted" delim_line_color="#c7c7c7"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_heading style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;" subtitle="Get started & get premium..."]A Different Class of Power BI Style Guides[/dfd_heading][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][vc_column_text css=""]

The Datalabs Agency offers two classes of Tableau Style Guides: Standard and Business Class. Does your company use Microsoft's Power BI? Check out our downloadable Power BI theme and templates.

It’s no longer about just reporting and analytics, but also about designing the best possible user experience for your audience. The Datalabs Agency understands the need for creativity in dashboard and report design – from what data to use, to the insights selected, to the final user experience (UX). Our Microsoft Power BI dashboard designers in Australia start with a simple idea: make intuitive, impactful dashboards that get answers visualized — memorably and beautifully.

We work with companies and government agencies across Australia and internationally — financial services, pharma, government, automotive, energy. In-person in Melbourne, or remotely anywhere.

We are not your stale, old-school consultancy. We think there’s more to designing effective dashboards than choosing a bar graph or a pie chart.

What are the Learning Outcomes of This Dashboard Training?

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]At the end of our end of the Designing Great Dashboards Workshop, you’ll have a process for designing your own BI dashboards, regardless of whether you use Excel, Tableau, or Power BI.
  • You'll be knowledgeable about how to arrive at higher-level insights and use new techniques to plan and execute a single BI dashboard.
  • Attendees will leave with a professional understanding of how data visualization, visual analytics, and user experience design combine to create useful and practical dashboards.
  • In addition, a portion of the workshop is dedicated to forming better business questions, questions that your dashboard's audience continuously asks (or should ask), and questions that will help simplify and glean insights from your data.
  • Attendees will then have the ability to prepare their own dashboard project, redesign/retrofit dashboards, and understand the power of users' feedback in the design process.
  • Finally, our facilitators will showcase new data visualization influences and resources that your team can use to inspire your next round of dashboard designs.

The Datalabs Agency brings data to life with beautiful interactivity. In our experience, the key to successful interactive data visualizations is the user experience (UX). Our interaction designers work with data journalists and data visualization developers to extract the meaningful and memorable insights from your data, constructing an experience that blows away standard 'flat' reporting, like PDFs or Word documents.

So treat your audience with respect. Value their time and intelligence. And turn your data and reports into digital charts and interactive visuals and see the benefits, visually.

Learn how to visualize data like a professional.

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]Data visualization is a powerful tool for telling stories with data. It can help us see patterns and trends that we might not have noticed otherwise, or tell a story in a way that’s more compelling than just numbers on a page. But it’s also hard work! There are so many different chart types out there, and each one has its own strengths and weaknesses. How do you choose the right one for your data? And once you pick the best type of graph, how does it fit inside your wider story? This workshop will teach attendees everything they need to know about visualizing their data effectively. Session rates are on our workshop pricing page.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_heading delimiter_settings="border-bottom-style:dotted;|border-bottom-width:1px;|width:100px;|border-bottom-color:#d2d2d2;" delimiter_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" style="style_02" subtitle="New methods and new thinking" title_font_options="tag:h2" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]

The art and science of turning raw information into lovely graphics

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]You will leave this workshop knowing how to simplify your data into something easy-to-understand; which chart types are useful for which kinds of datasets; how to highlight insights from your graphs; and finally, techniques for turning your visualizations into stories using graphic design software, like Canva or Adobe Illustrator. We know you might have early adopters in your teams and those who don't want to change.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_column_text css=""]This introductory workshop can be tailored for any audience at any level, for any industry: finance, government, healthcare, energy, or any other. Design Explainable Decisions with an AI expert.

This workshop is for government and corporate teams reporting on and communicating about AI.

What it is:

A fast-paced, hands-on workshop where agencies learn to turn AI-assisted decisions into clear, human-friendly explanations, backed by real governance checkpoints and transparency-ready visuals.

Why it’s useful & educational for you:

Learn visual storytelling and decision modelling as it relates to explainable AI . This workshop transforms explainability and AI compliance into a design challenge—mixing data visualisation, AI governance and dashboard prototyping.

Why is it a 'collaborative working session'?:

Participants visualize their AI registers, map their AI landscape, and then redesign those outputs in the training exercises for senior decision-makers or public consumption.

What is the XAI & AI Governance Workbook?:

Visualize. Decide. Explain. is the workbook for turning AI-assisted decisions into clear, confident, and compliance-ready stories.

The accompanying workshop walks you through mapping governance checkpoints, identifying risks, and creating visuals that meet Australia’s AI Technical Standard and Transparency Statement requirements.

Perfect for government teams, consultants, and decision-makers—download the abbreviated workbook now (form is located to the right) and imagine your AI explanation and governance commitments both getting clearer.

Get an AI consultant who can lead your team through collaborative working sessions that helps agencies meet DTA’s AI Technical Standard requirement for explainability, bias monitoring, and human oversight. title_responsive="line_height_mobile:10"]

The Project

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1761781529200{border-radius: 20px !important;}"]

The team at Walton Family Foundation reached out to Datalabs seeking assistance with a series of Tableau dashboards. The foundation behind the family that started Walmart was looking for sleek new designs for its major launch of new dashboards. The need for these dashboards was to present a series of metrics and KPIs on the environmental program for the foundation leadership team. These metrics were based on water quality, fish health, farming environmental impacts, and many more - all based on protecting the environment in America. The data for these metrics came from many sources. The first challenge was to sift through the data and design visualizations, and the second was to establish a data flow in Tableau to bring it to life. Read about how we did this below.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25693" img_size="full" style="vc_box_rounded"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner rtl_reverse="yes" css=".vc_custom_1648524807038{background-position: center !important;background-repeat: no-repeat !important;background-size: cover !important;}"][vc_column_inner width="1/2" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" responsive_styles="padding_top_mobile:20"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

The Design Phase

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]The data visualizer at Datalabs got straight to work with his design tool of choice, Figma. This is a great tool for producing dashboard prototypes and collaborating with others such as developers or the client themselves. Version control was an important factor as with so many metrics comes a lot of comments and a lot of design variations. Figma is a great way to see everything at once with multiple dashboards planted on the same pasteboard. After designing the color pallette, multiple charts, different layouts and even a couple otter icons, we managed to satisfy the team at WFF and move the designs into Tableau. See below.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25696" img_size="full" style="vc_box_rounded" css=".vc_custom_1648512105552{border-radius: 30px !important;}"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" responsive_styles="padding_top_mobile:20"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

The Tableau Development Phase

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]The Tableau phase was the longest as it became quite complex. The challenge was to design a simple Excel spreadsheet which allowed multiple users to enter and update data and feed that into Tableau through Tableau flow and prep builder. Our approach was to develop the dashboards and charts with dummy data first. This allowed us to establish a data structure that fed the variety of charts and provide WFF with a template to know the required data structure. Complex, I know. Well, put simply we developed the dashboards according to the designs to the tee and integrated the multiple data sources successfully. Now apart from being visually stunning, (if we do say so ourselves), they are completely interactive with dropdown filters and information tooltips.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25697" img_size="full" style="vc_box_rounded"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" responsive_styles="padding_top_mobile:20"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

The Final Outcome

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]This project had its challenges from juggling multiple data sources, multiple design versions, different user needs, etc. Yet, it was a success in the end and most importantly it hopefully assists in making our environment more sustainable and healthy. What made this project successful was clear and constant communication with the client. If challenges arose they were communicated and resolved as a group. At times, this meant the project process had to pivot slightly. Being agile and flexible with such a large and dynamic project is crucial and allowed these dashboards to be seen to the very end. Thanks to the team at Walton Family Foundation.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800"
