title_responsive="line_height_mobile:10"]

The Project

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1648772706196{border-radius: 20px !important;}"]

The fine folks at Michael and Susan Dell Foundation reached out to Datalabs with a unique Power BI design and development challenge. That was to re-design the education reporting system and migrate it from custom software to Power BI. The reporting system was to present and flag KPIs on learner and educator performance across schools in South Africa. The reporting system had many levels and users, visualizing data from a province high level down to individual student profiles. Therefore, the user experience navigating across views required a lot of thinking and design effort. We also took a slightly different design process for this particular project - read about it below.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25720" img_size="full" style="vc_box_rounded"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner rtl_reverse="yes" css=".vc_custom_1648524807038{background-position: center !important;background-repeat: no-repeat !important;background-size: cover !important;}"][vc_column_inner width="1/2" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" responsive_styles="padding_top_mobile:20"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

The Process

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]Our process began as usual with a kick-off meeting, (with stakeholders from America, South Africa and Australia). We then began the auditing of the current system, data and requirements/opportunities. Once we were happy with our audit, we presented the team at Dell a series of relational maps to define our system structure and have all parties on the same page. From here, this is where we changed up our process. We chose to design in Power BI! Thus the design and development were coinciding. This of course has the benefit of completing the project faster allowing for more time to add more features and the client being able to interact in the actual environment which is much better for technical and user testing. However, designing in Power BI rather than a design tool does have the risk of taking longer as it requires more time to develop than design. See below to see if this approach paid off.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25723" img_size="full" style="vc_box_rounded" css=".vc_custom_1648618713401{border-radius: 30px !important;}"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" responsive_styles="padding_top_mobile:20"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

The Power BI Development Phase

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]Designing in Power BI had both pros and cons. Let's start with the cons. In Power BI, the data defines how the charts look. To get a more accurate representation of how the charts will look in the final version, we had to create a lot of very specific dummy data. This took a lot of time. Plus, when there was a change, we had to do it all over again. Another set back was that Power BI was new software for the client, so they didn't know too much of the software capabilities and limitations. This inevitably meant Datalabs spent a lot of time documenting why decisions were made and why Power BI can't do certain functions. In retrospect, a lesson on Power BI would be good for clients less familiar at the start of the project. The benefits of designing in Power BI however was that we prototyped, experimented and tested all in the end software. From this we learnt so much and were able elements in that we likely wouldn't have before, such as the navigation system. Plus, the client got to interact with Power BI from an earlier stage which is fantastic for user feedback.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25697" img_size="full" style="vc_box_rounded"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C0.35)" responsive_styles="padding_top_mobile:20"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

The Final Outcome

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]Whilst this project saw a couple major challenges, the team at Datalabs overcame them and successfully produced a series of Power BI dashboards with heavy data sets and a complex user navigation system. The final result was four functional dashboards that acted as templates for a whole lot more. These dashboards are to be used by 10,958 unique users reporting data on 11.6M students across 22,732 schools! Well, the results are in. We recently received word from the team at the Dell Foundation that the dashboards have been a big hit. In particular the Overview page which we got told "has been a significant hit with our DDD users – they LOVE it." So all in all, a great project that we learnt a lot from.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" First, get the style in check

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1645684292949{border-radius: 20px !important;}"]

The team at Mercedes-Benz took the wise approach of beginning with defining a cohesive dashboard style before developing any dashboard. The Datalabs Agency took a collaborative approach injecting a lot of the Mercedes-Benz (or Daimler) brand and updating it to fit data visualization best practices. The icons, fonts and color palette all got extensive and worthwhile attention. Not to mention the choice of going to the dark side with dark backgrounds!

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480"][new_testimonials main_style="style-2" main_layout="layout-9" description="The Power BI style guide is very detailed and informative." title_font_options="tag:div" subtitle_font_options="tag:div" author="A Mercedes-Benz IT Developer" quote_color="#252525" content_font_options="font_size:14"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480"][vc_row_inner css=".vc_custom_1645497497390{background-position: center !important;background-repeat: no-repeat !important;background-size: cover !important;}"][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-right" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

We then set off for Singapore

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]For these large-scale projects, Zoom doesn't quite cut it. Perhaps it's the scent of testosterone in the room that makes the difference. Well, we were greeted upon arrival in Singapore and shuffled into a room with executives from both Asia and the headquarters in Stuttgart, Germany. It was no slow start with all excited about either explaining how the current planning dashboards work and the possibilities of what we can do with them. You can imagine how it went. There was people in the room geeking out on Power BI updates and others, such as myself, the style elements. We needed some order. See below.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25383" img_size="full" style="vc_box_rounded" css=".vc_custom_1645503255097{border-radius: 30px !important;}"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25384" img_size="full" style="vc_box_rounded"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

A new dashboard strategy and system

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]It took our Managing Director, Otto, to basically halt all conversations and mention reworking the dashboard strategy. It's worth mentioning that this is not why they flew us over. It was supposed to be for one sales dashboard concept but ended up turning into reinventing an entire networked sales system. Which all the best projects do. Once you hear Datalabs' ideas, it can be tough to say no. Next second, the general manager walks in the door and gets excited about onboarding us to assist in reimagine their dashboard strategy. The conversation became a lot more cohesive and collaborative with many dashboard ideas and solutions.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

The dashboards began rolling out

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]If you watched the video above, the total amount of dashboards exceeded 20. This sounds like a lot but remember the gigantic business that is Mercedes-Benz and what a new strategy would involve. Everything from planning tools, and competitor comparisons to on the showroom floor sales trackers. If this sounds cool, infuse it with a brand new style and you've definitely got me drooling. The style elements of these dashboards included black backgrounds, a vibrant and piercing blue chart color pallette, a number of actual Benz car icons and intuitive layouts that kept breaking protocol and paying off. Talk to us particularly about my favourite, the Stock and Production dashboard.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" Now used around the globe

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]Yes, you know that Mercedes-Benz dealership down the road from your place? Well, they'll be using our dashboard designs. The challenge here was to design a somewhat tailored experience for a global user base. We needed to design it to be very intuitive, fast loading, and set up for that specific dealership. We had a lot of key learnings from this especially around performance testing which we were constantly running diagnostics on. Apart from that, the large array of slicers needed work. We designed each dashboard to only have essential slicers and removed any unnecessary elements in the header to allow users to see the charts as quick as possible. Learning I now take into each new project.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

Designs for C-suite executives

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]We were dealing with executives feeding directly to the highest level positions at Mercedes-Benz. So, as you can imagine, we needed fast turnaround times. This meant we needed to perfect our process. We were well on top of file management with each of the 20 dashboards having 3 versions and multiple feedback documents. Nothing was lost. We were turning around dashboards quite fast also. This is a direct pay off from nailing down the style first and being in the room for the strategy discussions. We all knew the general plan and how to build it. These dashboards are now used by C-suite executives to drive sales decisions and track according to planning KPIs. Overall a very successful engagement and one we've learnt a lot from and will take into future projects.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_single_image image="25397" Superannuation is very competitive and therefore, very fast paced. Data and digital technology is growing rapidly in this sector. It’s time to not be left behind and in fact lead the way in sparking engagement, making business decisions and getting results through communication your data effectively. In this one day workshop, our experienced trainers will teach you a multiple range of design techniques which you are encouraged to apply through guided exercises throughout the day. The session covers a multitude of formats from PowerPoint presentations, to dashboards and interactive software. Get in touch with us to discuss how to tailor this workshop to a format of your choice, or leave it to us to take you through them all. Present data to the old with the techniques of the young!" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;"]Professional Training in Superannuation and Retirement specific Data Visualization & Storytelling[/dfd_heading][/dfd_equal_height_content][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" css=".vc_custom_1635917848307{padding-right: 6% !important;padding-left: 6% !important;background-color: #252525 !important;}" responsive_styles="padding_left_desktop:30|padding_right_desktop:30|padding_left_tablet:30|padding_right_tablet:30|padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="59" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="50"][dfd_heading title_google_fonts="yes" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" style="style_02" subtitle="Up-skill your team in the creative, visual communications for the superannuation and retirement sector. In this one day training, the Datalabs Agency will provide you and your colleagues with all of the tools required to produce something that is easy to analyse, creates engagement and is set up to provide you insights and recommended actions. The insurance industry is one that has more data than most. Through design exercises, we’ll guide you through our process of managing and reducing heavy datasets and reports into quick attention grabbing summaries. Be it as an infographic or a BI dashboard. Such data needs to be visualised to best design standards to identify and understand patterns, correlations and trends in order to make correct medical and possible life saving decisions. We at Datalabs Agency have had experience designing and training in the healthcare and science industry for a number of clients, (scroll down to see). We’ll take all of our knowledge and share it with you, through theory, guided exercises and open discussions. This workshop is customizable and can focus on a format of your choosing, being dashboards, infographics, interactive applications or all of the above. With such a large amount of data flooding into healthcare organizations, it is time to get in front of it. Get in touch with the Datalabs Agency to get started!" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;"]Professional Training for Data Visualization & Storytelling in the Healthcare Industry[/dfd_heading][/dfd_equal_height_content][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" css=".vc_custom_1635915625020{padding-right: 6% !important;padding-left: 6% !important;background-color: #252525 !important;}" responsive_styles="padding_left_desktop:30|padding_right_desktop:30|padding_left_tablet:30|padding_right_tablet:30|padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="59" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="50"][dfd_heading title_google_fonts="yes" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" style="style_02" subtitle="Up-skill your team in the creative, visual communications for the Healthcare industry. pages/19401.content:
[vc_row dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content" css=".vc_custom_1581310132524{padding-right: 0px !important;padding-left: 0px !important;}"][vc_column][rev_slider alias="investment-banking"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" css=".vc_custom_1635912895011{padding-right: 6% !important;padding-left: 6% !important;background-color: #252525 !important;}" responsive_styles="padding_left_desktop:40|padding_right_desktop:40|padding_left_tablet:40|padding_right_tablet:40|padding_left_mobile:30|padding_right_mobile:30"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="50" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][dfd_equal_height_content columns_width="half-size-elements" columns_offsets="dfd-normal-paddings" align_content_vertically="yes" mobile_destroy_equal_heights="yes"][videoplayer main_style="style-1" video_link="https://youtu.be/dErsZKdKGl8" title_font_options="tag:h3|color:%23ffffff" subtitle_font_options="tag:div|color:%23ffffff" title="Data Visualization for Investment Banking" subtitle="A bit about the Workshop" icon_color="#0a0a0a" icon_bg_color="#000000"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" enable_delimiter="" title_google_fonts="yes" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:32|color:%23ffffff|line_height:40|letter_spacing:1" subtitle_font_options="tag:h5|font_size:20|color:%23ffffff|line_height:28|letter_spacing:1" subtitle="As an Investment Banker, you don’t just need to know how to visualise data but need to know how to communicate opportunities and present growth. The Datalabs Agency will take you through our bullet-proof process to ensure those valuable insights are communicated effectively to stakeholders. This is done through understanding how to visualise data, how to tell a story with that data and how to set up a dashboard that can run on pilot mode presenting you with insights as they arise. We will take you through our solutions with past Investment Banking clients which you can immediately apply to your own dashboards, reports and presentations and cause positive disruption. There will be guided exercises, presentations and coffee breaks throughout also. You don’t want to be left behind. There are many data visualization possibilities within this sector from storytelling with infographics to designing interactive dashboards. The Datalabs Agency are now providing a full day workshop providing an introduction to data visualization specific to human resources. The day covers topics such as best practice in charts and diagrams and what formats and processes a HR employee can take to communicate data to the best effect. There are possibilities to further tailor the workshop to your organization by focusing more on a specific format, presenting your current style guide and using your own data in exercises. Now’s the best time to get ahead of the game with a Datalabs Agency data visualization workshop." heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;"]Professional Training on Data Visualization Tailored Specifically for Human Resources Employees[/dfd_heading][/dfd_equal_height_content][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" css=".vc_custom_1635912482388{padding-right: 6% !important;padding-left: 6% !important;background-color: #252525 !important;}" responsive_styles="padding_left_desktop:30|padding_right_desktop:30|padding_left_tablet:30|padding_right_tablet:30|padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="59" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="50"][dfd_heading title_google_fonts="yes" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" style="style_02" subtitle="Up-skill your team in the creative, visual communications for human resources. Whether it’s communicating data trends to others or analysing it yourself. In our visualizing corporate finance data training, The Datalabs Agency will take your current methods to the next level. Learn how to apply our tried and tested process to ensure your data presentations will be engaged with and your reports easier to understand. Throughout the day, we will look at data visualization from multiple angles, being the graphic design elements, storytelling methods and format applications to name a few. The whole day will be finance specific, from the theory, the examples and the exercises. If you’re considering something like this could be good for your company, please get in touch to see how we can tailor it even more!" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;"]Professional Training on Data Visualization Tailored Specifically for Corporate Finance Employees[/dfd_heading][/dfd_equal_height_content][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" css=".vc_custom_1635917627252{padding-right: 6% !important;padding-left: 6% !important;background-color: #252525 !important;}" responsive_styles="padding_left_desktop:30|padding_right_desktop:30|padding_left_tablet:30|padding_right_tablet:30|padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="59" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="50"][dfd_heading title_google_fonts="yes" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" style="style_02" subtitle="Up-skill your team in creative, visual communications for corporate finance specific data. For example, visualizing patterns can present opportunities you may not have been aware of or setting up a sales funnel to see where customers are dropping off. Sales is a certain field with a substantially large influx of data coming from multiple sources, which can be difficult to manage and understand. With a Datalabs Agency training workshop, you’ll be guided through theory and exercises to not only manage such data but strategically use it to present opportunities, risks and much more. This workshop can also be customised to use your own sales data and deep dive into a format of your choosing. title_font_options="tag:h5|font_size:18|color:%23ffffff|line_height:32|letter_spacing:0.5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]Get the confidence to influence and entertain your audience. It all starts with designing your data well and using storytelling to make it memorable. At the Datalabs Agency, we believe that, in the proper hands, Microsoft PowerPoint could be used for the purposes of good, rather than evil! PowerPoint and those that have used it badly have a lot to answer for…This workshop is here to set things right, to train and inspire teams of non-designers in creative data presentations and visual storytelling. We teach the techniques we use in our day-to-day agency life to tell stories will stay in the minds of the audience long after the presentation has ended. Data is believable. Which Type of Data Visualization Are You Interested in Learning About?

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]

In this article, let's look at the different types of data visualization.

[/vc_column_text][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-12" width="1/6" offset="vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-12" width="4/6" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" offset="vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-8 vc_col-xs-10" css=".vc_custom_1507277465182{padding-right: 0px !important;padding-left: 0px !important;}" responsive_styles="padding_left_tablet:20|padding_right_tablet:20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_column_text]

What charts are out there in the world? What formats are used in modern data visualization? What types of tools and software do you use for data visualization?

I wanted to know the answer when I started designing data. And this industry is always changing, year after year. So we've refreshed our view on the different chart types we think you should know about. We've expanded into the different formats data visualization is viewed and experienced. And finally, if you're interested in "how-to" visualize data, click on the button below to peek inside the types of data visualization tools you want to be aware of in 2022. Types of Data Visualization Charts and Graphs

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text]

With the growing amount and accessibility of data, knowledge about the types of data visualization is becoming increasingly important. According to the writers of A Tour Through the Visualization Zoo, “The goal of visualization is to aid our understanding of data by leveraging the human visual system's highly-tuned ability to see patterns, spot trends, and identify outliers.”

 

In general, there are two different types of data visualization: exploration, which helps find a story the data is telling you, and an explanation, which tells a story to an audience. Both types of data visualization must take into account the audience’s expectations. Within these two basic categories, there are many different ways data can be made visual. In this article, we’ll go through the 15 most common types of data visualization that fall under the 2D area, temporal, multidimensional, hierarchical, and network categories.
